findings.title: Provider holes are exempted without checking the dataset condition
findings.description: `not_caught_up_report` skips every `provider_hole` session. The cutover’s stated exception is narrower: a provider hole is exempt only on a provider-missing day. The status logic likewise considers a provider hole caught up only when `provider_missing` is true. A hole on an available or degraded day can therefore be omitted from the not-caught-up evidence and exit checks.

findings.title: The estimate’s 30-day ceiling command omits unheld provider spend
findings.description: The printed command derives its 30-day cap from `planned_usd` and `trailing_30d_usd`, but the purchase guard also includes the estimate’s `unheld_jobs` in its 30-day spend calculation. If an unheld job pushes the required cap past the next $5 step, the command printed for the PM will still leave the full cutover refused. Include that spend when deriving the cap.

findings.title: The slice argument can escape the notes directory
findings.description: `_nonempty` accepts arbitrary non-whitespace strings, and `slice_id` is interpolated into state-file and log paths. A value containing path components (for example, `../...`) can direct those writes outside `NOTES_DIR`. Since the argument is documented as a slice number, validate it as such or otherwise reject path separators and traversal components.

findings.title: Cross-tier over-session names lose their family
findings.description: `over_sessions` extracts names from coverage checks without retaining each check’s `family`, and the evidence collector groups the names only by product. `over_failures` then attaches that same product-wide list to each family’s over count. When multiple volume families have over sessions, the evidence can attribute a session to the wrong family. Preserve the family in the collected names and match it to the corresponding accounting row.
